query: Consider the following context: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) exhibit excellent properties such as high strength, good ductility, superior corrosion resistance, and thermal stability, making them highly promising for applications in the aerospace, energy, and automotive industries. Among them, the FeNiCrMn HEA demonstrates outstanding corrosion resistance while eliminating the expensive Co element present in the “Cantor” alloy, significantly reducing costs. However, current research on the FeNiCrMn HEA has primarily focused on its corrosion resistance, with relatively limited studies on its mechanical properties. In that context, which method can be used for the stated problem, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Processing FeNiCrMn high‐entropy alloy using a rapid consolidation technique such as Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) will yield a bulk material with a refined microstructure that exhibits enhanced mechanical properties compared to conventionally cast samples.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrMn HEA obtained either by traditional casting or from mechanically alloyed powders.
generation.intervention: Consolidation of the alloy powders into dense bulk samples via SPS, followed by standard mechanical tests (e.g., compression and/or tensile testing).
generation.conditions: Room temperature testing under quasi-static loading conditions, ensuring samples are produced with minimal residual stress and fine grain structure.
generation.structural_mediator: The refined grain structure and reduced residual stresses achieved by the rapid sintering process.
generation.mechanism: SPS’s rapid heating and pressure application promote densification and grain refinement while limiting coarsening and undesirable phase formation. These microstructural improvements can enhance dislocation motion resistance, leading to higher yield strength and ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: The SPS-processed FeNiCrMn HEA is predicted to show higher yield strength and better ductility compared with conventionally cast samples, indicating improved mechanical performance.
generation.baseline: Conventional as-cast FeNiCrMn HEA samples, which typically exhibit coarser grain structures and higher residual stresses that can limit mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: The degree of improvement may depend on specific SPS parameters (e.g., heating rate, pressure, holding time) and could be less pronounced if minor oxide inclusions or processing-induced defects are present.
generation.uncertainty: While the overall trend toward mechanical improvement is expected, the precise magnitude of strength and ductility enhancement remains uncertain without dedicated experimental optimization and verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeNiCrMn HEA samples: one set consolidated via SPS and a control set produced via conventional casting. Characterize their microstructure with SEM/TEM for grain size and residual stress analysis. Perform standardized compression and/or tensile tests to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SPS-processed samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical properties (higher strength, enhanced ductility) and refined microstructure compared to the conventionally processed samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties

Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.
